questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university's reputation in my area of study (physics)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A little "bureaucratic", but very much a joy.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy, everything was sent by mail

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Assistance from the host university's international office with forms and course selection.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite challenging, but that is mostly attributable to the housing situation in Munich.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Start applying for housing well in advance. The website "WG-gesucht" worked well for me, although I would be wary of whether the landlord offers official address registration.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: At times the procedure is a little "opaque", but it was simple in the end.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
- Fill out forms.
- Pay the mandatory fee.
- Upload an image for your student card.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international office was in general very helpful if there was any questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very. In my situation, I was even able to register for a class in the neighboring university.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The biggest surprise to me was how late one could register for courses, and even later for exams. In Munich, one is able to try out various courses before officially registering.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Two master courses (19 ECTS) and the rest bachelors (15 ECTS).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Generally loose, and very much up to the lecturers discretion how the course is taught and at what level. This does give some variability in difficulty - some are very easy, some are very hard. Independence in study habit is also more needed at LMU as compared to UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
General Relativity
Quantum field theory (at Technische Universität)
IUCM german course
Physics communication
Introduction to machine learning

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Quantum field theory (at TUM) and physics communication where both great. General Relativity too, although I believe there will be a different lecturer next semester.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: University registration fee

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transport is very cheap (get the Deutschland ticket with student discount)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great student sport facility (ZHS)

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
ZHS offers various courses for sports, including tours to the alps for climbing.

The IUCM German course (and the excursions they offer) was also a great intro to the city, area and university.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking - with a Deutschland ticket, one can get to the alps and back for free with about two hours each way.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Oktoberfest if possible, the alps, the museums, neighboring cities.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Bierstube close to Olympiazentrum is a great place to grab a beer. Otherwise the various Biergarten's or Bierhaus's are also fun.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Emphasis on studying.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Course structures and registrations are very loose as compared to UCPH, take advantage of that (try out courses before committing)
2) Make sure to meet some people early, it is harder to meet new people during the semester.
3) Be aware of the shifted semester dates - make a plan ahead of time of how to catch up with courses at UCPH after the exchange.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be well prepared for the exams, some can be hard, and one has to emphasize speed when solving problems.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning the courses, and hikes.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Taking the Quantum Field Theory course.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
